reason: (1) Over Z/r (r large prime) rank B needs >= B relations regardless of distribution; the excess above B is coverage-dominated (coupon collector, ~B ln B/(m+1) rows for uniform weights), and uniform column weights MINIMIZE the cover time; any degree-variance shaping increases relations needed. k-XORSAT thresholds are an F_2 / fixed-density phenomenon and do not lower the B lower bound. (2) Column hit distribution is set by which factor-base points occur in decompositions, i.e. by the group law + summation-cover membership, not by choice of F beyond the mean (monodromy fixes it); the algorithm remains group-op-plus-membership, so CGK B*D^2 >= N applies unchanged. (3) Linear algebra is not the bottleneck stage; at best constant factor <= ln B, accounting only.

data.sim: B=1024, 3-uniform rows, random coeffs mod 65521, incremental rank to full
